title: Values and types — the Vyrn guide

chapter.title: Values and types
chapter.lede: Numbers state their width. Text is UTF-8 bytes. A type can carry the rule that makes a value valid, and the compiler checks the rule where it can.

sections.heading: Numbers
prose: Every number type states its width: Int8, Int16, Int32, Int64, the unsigned pairs, Float32 and Float64. There is no unsized Int, because its width would then depend on the machine.
A conversion is written. Int64(x) widens, and nothing widens on its own.

sections.heading: Text
prose: A String is UTF-8 bytes. byteLength is a field and counts bytes; charCount() walks the string and counts characters. The two agree on ASCII and disagree everywhere else, and the names say which one you asked for.
std/strings has the rest: split, join, trim, case, search, pad.

sections.heading: Validated types
prose: A where clause is part of the type. Age(30) is proven while the file compiles, so no check is emitted. Age(5) is refused by the compiler, in the same way a type error is refused.

Input from outside the program is not a constant, so it gets the total form. Age?(n) answers Option<Age>: Some when the rule holds, None when it does not. Nothing traps, and you cannot forget a check you never wrote.
The rule is readable by the compiler as well as by you. Chapter 9 turns the same declaration into a JSON Schema document.
